kinds.demo-seed: First-run demo fixtures (a starter file tree, playlist, photo set, threads, calendars, reminders, voice memos, contacts). Written **only when the store key is absent**, so an intentionally emptied store stays empty (each app pins that with a 'not re-seeded' test). Two of these files (Calendar, Reminders) also carry a second, different write on the same key: repairing a *missing built-in* calendar/list, because rows under it would otherwise be unreachable — that happens while the key exists and inserts only the built-in entry, never re-seeding demo content. A rejected seed write costs nothing lasting: the app re-derives the fixture on the next mount and no screen claims it was stored.
kinds.system-event-removed: RETIRED (REQ-A150, round 86). This kind used to classify the incoming-call append in `src/svelte/IncomingCall.svelte` as an accepted *residual gap* ('a rejected write costs that one history row, silently'), because the call overlay is closing and no screen is left to report a failure. That is no longer true of the code: the append is now a checked write whose rejected row is queued in memory (`queuePendingCall`) and flushed by the Phone screen's history — which is also where the user would look for it — with an honest notice while it is still pending. The gate reported this entry stale (`shrink with a reason`), which is how the retirement became visible. Recorded here (not deleted silently) because the *reason* a classification disappears is part of the audit trail. The retired reason was: "Content appended when the *platform* reports an event (a finished incoming call is appended to the call log). There is n…"
kinds.derived-tick: Derived, self-healing state written by a background tick (marking alarms as `ringing`). It is not a user edit and no screen claims it was stored; a rejected write only degrades the ring UI until the next tick recomputes it.
kinds.store-seam: The store seam itself (`lib/amosStore.ts`): the single place that owns the localStorage write, the Rust `store_set` write-through, the failure report and the `amos-store-changed` event.
kinds.raw-string-store: A raw-string store that deliberately does **not** use the JSON seam: `theme`/`locale`/AI-session-id values are plain strings read at boot (before the JSON layer exists) and written by non-JS consumers, so encoding them as JSON would break the readers. Each mirrors to the Rust `store_set` like the seam does.
kinds.host-mirror: The cross-window mirror inside `svelte/store.ts`: it applies a payload the **host** declared authoritative (`store-updated`), so it must not write back through the seam (that would echo the host's own value) — it writes localStorage and updates its own writable.
kinds.session-id: The AI conversation id (`lib/backend.ts`): a plain-string pointer to the current multi-turn session, read/written as a raw string for the same reason as the other raw stores. Classified `derived` in `scripts/store-allowlist.json`, so it is intentionally not part of a backup.
